name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in read-only mode for one week. This lets us collect real data on how often it flags issues without disrupting teams. The trade-off is slower feedback loops, but we avoid breaking builds or frustrating developers during the observation period. After the week, we’ll enforce rules only where the data shows clear value.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just slower feedback—it’s that dry-run normalizes noise. PR-Agent’s false positives will clutter PRs, training teams to ignore it, so when we enforce rules later, they’ll distrust every flag. Instead, run a targeted pilot on one repo with strict thresholds; if it flags nothing useful in a week, scrap it. Settle this with hard data: measure false-positive rate and dev ignore rate before and after.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in read-only mode on a single repo for one week first, then expand to all repos only if the false-positive rate stays below 5%. This cuts the observation period in half while still measuring real-world noise before full deployment.
